title: youthful dutch floral tagine
description: a cozy, velvety dutch dish featuring vin-santo and tagine-cooked vegetables, suitable for breakfast or dessert
instructions: Combine the almond milk, dried rose petals, and dried orange blossoms in a saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture steep for 10 minutes.
Strain the mixture into a blender and add the vanilla extract, vin-santo, coconut sugar, and tahini.
Blend the mixture until smooth and creamy.
Return the mixture to the saucepan and add the flaxseed meal.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens.
Pour the tagine into individual serving cups or ramekins.
Refrigerate the tagine until chilled, at least 2 hours.
Serve the tagine chilled, garnished with additional dried rose petals or orange blossoms if desired.
